newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Defense Secretary to visit Europe, Gulf.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Defense Secretary to visit Europe, Gulf.

text.p: U.S. Defence William Cohen will attend a NATO meeting in Belgium and visit Saudi Arabia and four other Gulf states on a trip beginning next week, the Defence Department said on Thursday.

Cohen will attend a meeting of Atlantic alliance defence ministers in Brussels on June 12-13 and then go to Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Bahrain, the United Arab Emirates and Oman before returning to Washington on June 18, the Pentagon said.

The visit to the Gulf region will be "in an effort to get to know members of the Gulf Cooperation Council, and also to meet with American troops in the area," Defense Department spokesman Ken Bacon told reporters.

It will be Cohen's first visit as secretary to the Gulf, where the United States maintains a major naval presence based in Bahrain as well as a fleet of warplanes in Saudi Arabia and Kuwait which keep watch over southern Iraq.

Defense officials said privately that the Gulf trip was a get-acquainted visit and that they did not expect any final report from Saudi Arabia on two car bombings in the kingdom since late 1995 that have killed a total of 24 U.S. troops stationed there.

In addition to meeting Gulf leaders, Cohen is expected to visit some 5,000 U.S. troops who were moved to a remote desert airbase in Saudi Arabia after the second car bombing at Dhahran on June 25 of last year which killed 19 American airmen.
